'''''Euphorbia paniculata''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the spurge family [[Euphorbiaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to the [[Iberian Peninsula]] and [[North Africa]] in the western [[Mediterranean Basin]].

==Description==
[[File:Euphorbia paniculata Enfoque 2011-4-21 SierraMadrona.jpg|thumb|left|Leaves]]
''Euphorbia paniculata'' is a perennial plant up to {{convert|1.5|m|abbr=on}} tall. It has a woody, thickened stock with erect stems, woody at the base with up to 11 fertile lateral branches. Leaves are green, {{convert|25|-|100|x|10|-|25|mm}}, elliptical to lanceolate, sessile, generally amplexicaul with serrulate or entire margins. It has non-appendiculate yellow nectaries and ellipsoidal, black seeds.<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=Euphorbia paniculata |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/08_108_06%20Euphorbia.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=30 March 2021}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Euphorbia paniculata'' is native to the southwestern [[Iberian Peninsula]], northern [[Morocco]] and the northern coastline of [[Algeria]] and [[Tunisia]]. It inhabits forests and humid [[shrubland]], in troughs and next to temporary waterways.<ref name="iberica" />
